The company recognized $382 million in 2023 from fabrication facility underutilization due to wafer start reductions and estimates an additional $200 million in period costs from underutilization in the first quarter of 2024.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company has proprietary fabrication facilities; inability to utilize them fully could result in fixed costs not being absorbed, leading to higher average unit costs and lower gross margins.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AVGO discuss the operational risks and financial impacts associated with manufacturing facility utilization. MU reports that it has proactively lowered its structural wafer capacity by redeploying equipment and reducing wafer starts, resulting in high utilization on remaining high-volume nodes and reduced underutilization charges. In contrast, AVGO discusses the risk that if it is unable to utilize its proprietary fabrication facilities at a desired level, the fixed costs will not be absorbed, leading to higher average unit costs and lower gross margins. While MU describes a managed reduction leading to efficiency, AVGO highlights the passive risk of underutilization affecting margins.

sentences.text: In manufacturing, we have been fully utilized throughout most of 2024 on our high-volume manufacturing nodes where we are maximizing output against our current capacity, which we have proactively, structurally lowered.
Since the number of wafer processing steps is higher for leading-edge nodes, this approach has resulted in a meaningful structural reduction in DRAM and NAND wafer capacity.
Subsequently, fabrication facility underutilization was reduced and principally related to legacy manufacturing capacity.
Although we outsource a significant portion of our manufacturing activities, we do have some proprietary semiconductor fabrication facilities.

If we are unable to utilize our owned fabrication facilities at a desired level, the fixed costs associated with these facilities will not be fully absorbed, resulting in higher average unit costs and lower gross margins.

comparisons.peer_topic: R&D, Product Development, and Construction Execution Risks
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel faces significant risks in its R&D and product development, including potential delays, lower-than-anticipated yields, and defect challenges in developing new process nodes and disaggregated designs, as evidenced by past delays in 10nm, 7nm, and Xeon releases. These technical risks are compounded by construction project risks involving labor, materials, and regulatory constraints, as well as production disruptions from errors, material defects, or equipment issues. High capital expenditures for advanced manufacturing and facilities, combined with potential demand decreases or failure to forecast accurately, create risks of margin pressure, asset impairments (such as the $3.1 billion charge in Q3 2024), and write-offs, highlighting the financial exposure inherent in these execution challenges.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and INTC disclose financial consequences related to manufacturing capacity and process technology transitions. MU states that its structural capacity reduction involved redeploying equipment to leading-edge nodes, which reduced wafer processing steps, and notes that underutilization was reduced. INTC discusses how adapting designs for new manufacturing processes involves additional R&D expense, higher costs due to advanced capital equipment utilization, and results in unused manufacturing capacity charges (specifically citing a $3.1 billion charge in Q3 2024). Both companies link leading-edge node transitions to complex capacity dynamics and financial impacts, though MU focuses on a successful structural reduction while INTC highlights execution risks and impairment charges.

sentences.text: In addition, to improve capital efficiency, we redeployed equipment from older technology nodes to support conversions to leading-edge nodes.
Since the number of wafer processing steps is higher for leading-edge nodes, this approach has resulted in a meaningful structural reduction in DRAM and NAND wafer capacity.
Subsequently, fabrication facility underutilization was reduced and principally related to legacy manufacturing capacity.

This has in the past and may in the future result in higher operating costs, including as a result of additional costs from unused manufacturing capacity, higher leverage and borrowing costs, and pressure on our credit ratings, and adversely affect our business, financial condition and prospects.

For example, adapting a processor or component design for a new or different manufacturing process involves additional R&D expense and can result in delays in the development of the associated product and higher costs due to the utilization of more advanced and expensive capital equipment.

Both companies identify leading-edge node transitions as a significant operational and financial driver, with MU focusing on capacity structure and QCOM on input cost increases.
